builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Stochastic Pruning of the DPO Computation Graph: 1.4x Faster Training and Lower Peak Memory
summary: The method replaces the standard concatenated DPO training step with stochastic sampling of scored response positions, executed prefixes, and backpropagated preference branches, omitting the corresponding computation before it occurs. It costs a modified training objective (partially corrected with inverse-probability weighting for single-branch gradients), added implementation complexity in the training loop, and slightly lower mean accuracy with benchmark-dependent changes in open-ended generation scores. It can fail if the accuracy degradation is unacceptable for the target task, if the claimed savings do not transfer beyond the two model families evaluated, or if the unbiased estimator's higher variance destabilizes convergence on the reader's data distribution.
rationale: The speedup and memory savings are directly relevant to a 24 GB GPU fine-tuning workflow, but the measured quality trade-off and limited evaluation breadth require validation on the reader's own preference data before production adoption.
technique: Stochastic pruning of DPO computation graph

claims.statement: The method replaces the standard concatenated DPO training step with stochastic sampling of scored response positions, executed prefixes, and backpropagated preference branches, omitting the corresponding computation before it occurs. It costs a modified training objective (partially corrected with inverse-probability weighting for single-branch gradients), added implementation complexity in the training loop, and slightly lower mean accuracy with benchmark-dependent changes in open-ended generation scores. It can fail if the accuracy degradation is unacceptable for the target task, if the claimed savings do not transfer beyond the two model families evaluated, or if the unbiased estimator's higher variance destabilizes convergence on the reader's data distribution.
Branch pruning yields a 1.426x step-time speedup over concatenated DPO and reduces total training time by about 30% relative to stock DPO; position and sequence pruning primarily reduce peak memory.
